reader.requirement: At --std 85 a report group description entry's data-name-1, when written, must immediately follow the level-number (a name written after any clause refused), and every other clause of formats 1-3 must be accepted in any sequence with the same effect, each at most once; the witness covers one reordered entry.

FILLER as a report entry name and the multiple COLUMN form are refused below 2002 (COBOL0900); not the order path

reader.edition-search: the entryNameHere predicate and reportGroupClause* consult no edition (grep DialectLevel in CobolReportWriter.g4 actions: none)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the order; 85 has a smaller clause set (no FILLER name, no PRESENT WHEN, no VARYING, no multiple COLUMN)

reader.notes: reportGroupEntry takes the optional dataName only right after levelNumber (guarded by entryNameHere), and reportGroupBody is reportGroupClause*, so a name after a clause has no production; ClosedFormatPass counts each clause once with no order rank.

refuter.evidence: The 1985 SUM clause prints {SUM {identifier-2}... [UPON ...]}..., so SUM may be written more than once within one clause. RGA.cob tests this alongside entry names that are reserved only in later editions: 03 PRESENT COLUMN 1 PIC 999 SUM N SUM M, and 03 CENTER PIC 999 SUM N UPON DE-G SUM M COLUMN 5, and 03 COLS COLUMN 9 ... VALUE. It compiles and runs at 85. The report line is '031 031 OK' (N=3+8, M=10+10), so the cardinality screen does not count a repeated SUM phrase as a repeated clause, and a 2002-reserved word in the name slot is taken as data-name-1. RGB.cob writes RESET ON FINAL before SUM (RESET is a phrase of the SUM clause, not a free clause) and is refused with COBOL0001 unexpected 'RESET'. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.9.3 SR2  (3.9.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'.
